solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique after crossings); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Charm shown by publication — new version of Times

parts.note: a mag is a magazine, an everyday publication

indicators.note: a new version of a word rearranges its letters, so these letters are reordered

explanation.surface: A newspaper's charm lies in its fresh edition of The Times.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Times' looks like the newspaper's name but is just anagram fodder; 'new' supplies its own N first.
explanation.definitionFit: Magnetism is personal attraction, a close synonym of charm in the sense of appeal.

clue.text: Novel, revolutionary trouble for old ruler

indicators.note: something revolutionary turns over, so the novel's title is read backwards

explanation.surface: A novel about revolutionary unrest brings trouble to an ancient monarch.
explanation.walkthrough: Kim is Kipling's 1901 novel of a boy in British India.
explanation.definitionFit: The Mikado was the title given to the emperor of Japan, now historical.

clue.text: Supervisor for hunting a bird in green space

indicators.note: the bird phrase is placed inside the word for the green space

parts.note: a garden is a green space

explanation.surface: Someone who oversees hunting spots a bird in a park.
explanation.walkthrough: A mew (or sea mew) is a gull; the garden opens after its G to take it in.
explanation.definitionFit: A gamewarden is an official who oversees hunting and protects wild animals on an estate or reserve.

clue.text: Surviving tours United left jubilant

indicators.note: to tour something is to go round it, so the surviving word goes round the other letters

explanation.surface: A survivor travels round after United leave, overjoyed.
explanation.definitionFit: Exultant means triumphantly happy, the same feeling as jubilant.

clue.text: Keen on drinking whiskey, thus something may get broken?

definitions.note: an adverbial phrase: the manner in which something breaks

indicators.note: drinking takes something in, so the whiskey letter goes inside

parts.note: to be into something is to be keen on it
W is whiskey in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: Someone fond of whiskey may end up breaking something.
explanation.definitionFit: A thing broken in two is split into two pieces, which is how something may get broken.

clue.text: It looks like this — foreign character oddly missing clothes

indicators.note: to clothe is to cover, so the rearranged letters wrap round the Greek letter
behaving oddly means out of normal order, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: nu is a letter of the Greek alphabet

explanation.surface: A dash points to a foreign figure strangely without clothes.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue's dash is the definition's 'this': a dash looks like the sign for subtraction.
explanation.definitionFit: The subtraction symbol is a short horizontal stroke, just like the dash printed in the clue.

clue.text: Poor area by Rio? Preferred North American city

parts.note: a fave is a favourite, the preferred one

explanation.surface: Choosing between a poor district of Rio and a favourite American city.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that Rio de Janeiro is only one example.
explanation.definitionFit: A favela is a Brazilian shanty town, the slums found on the hills around Rio.

clue.text: President hasn't finished drink

indicators.note: a word that is not finished loses its last letter

parts.note: the chair of a meeting is its president

explanation.surface: The president has not drunk all their drink.
explanation.definitionFit: Chai is spiced tea, the Indian name for the beverage.

clue.text: Unripped condition of letter

definitions.meaning: first meaning, read cryptically: free of rents, or tears
second meaning: a letting where no rent is charged

explanation.walkthrough: 'Letter' is not something posted but one who lets property; 'rent' also means a tear.
explanation.definitionFit: A rent-free arrangement lets someone occupy property without paying; whimsically, free of rents means without tears.

clue.text: Penning front part, I prepare the ground for story

indicators.note: to pen something is to enclose it, so the front part goes inside

parts.note: to hoe is to break up soil
the van is the vanguard, the front

explanation.surface: A gardener writes a story while working the soil.
explanation.definitionFit: Ivanhoe is Sir Walter Scott's historical novel, a story of medieval England.

clue.text: Without hesitation, king and queen hate peeled fruit

indicators.note: in its old sense of outside, so king and queen sit outside the hesitation

parts.note: um is a sound of hesitation

indicators.note: a peeled word loses its outer letters

explanation.surface: A royal couple promptly declares their loathing of skinned fruit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Without hesitation' reads as 'promptly', but 'without' means outside.
explanation.definitionFit: A kumquat is a small citrus fruit eaten whole, peel and all.

clue.text: Modernist's material coming from the east

indicators.note: in an across answer, coming from the east means read from right to left

explanation.surface: A modernist writer's fabric is imported from the East.
explanation.definitionFit: T. S. Eliot was a leading poet of literary Modernism, author of The Waste Land.

clue.text: Strike idiots on behind

indicators.note: on means placed next to, so idiots come after behind

parts.note: a team that is behind is down
a tool is slang for a fool

explanation.surface: Fools set their sights on someone's bottom.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Behind' looks like the backside but means trailing, as in two goals down.
explanation.definitionFit: Workers who down tools stop work in protest, the same as going on strike.

clue.text: In front of monarch, blow kiss

indicators.note: the blow word comes before the monarch

explanation.surface: Someone blows a kiss before the monarch.
explanation.walkthrough: ER, Elizabeth Regina, stands for the Queen; smacker is slang for a loud kiss.
explanation.definitionFit: A smacker is slang for a hearty, noisy kiss on the lips.

clue.text: Cryptic indication of red potato

definitions.meaning: the word red can be built as R, a king, then ED, short for Edward
the answer is also a variety of potato with red patches on its skin

explanation.walkthrough: This is a reverse clue: the answer is what a setter might write to clue RED, since R is king and ED short for Edward.
explanation.definitionFit: King Edward is a well-known British potato variety, white with pink-red blushes on its skin.

clue.text: Sky features return of popular doctor, upright character

indicators.note: a return goes back, so the popular word is read backwards

parts.note: MB is a medical degree, Bachelor of Medicine
the letter I is a single upright stroke

explanation.surface: Features in the sky signal the comeback of a well-liked, honest doctor.
explanation.definitionFit: Nimbi are rain clouds, or haloes, so they are things seen in the sky.

clue.text: It increases volume of e.g. a diamond around ring

indicators.note: turning around reverses order, so a gem is read backwards

parts.note: a diamond is an example of a gem, with the article supplying A
to ring someone is to phone them

explanation.surface: Something that adds bulk to a diamond, perhaps the setting around a ring.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Volume' suggests size or bulk, but it means loudness.
explanation.definitionFit: A megaphone is a cone that amplifies the voice, making it louder.

clue.text: Forces newbie into ill-fated action the wrong way

indicators.note: read the wrong way means backwards
the letters sit inside the phrase, so they are taken from within it

explanation.surface: A new recruit is drawn into a doomed operation that goes wrong.
explanation.definitionFit: A cadet is a trainee in the armed forces or police, a newcomer to service life.

clue.text: Officer, before mass trouble in the rear, does my job

indicators.note: before places the officer's letters ahead of the mass and the trouble that follow

parts.note: piles, haemorrhoids, are a painful complaint of the bottom

explanation.surface: An officer with a sore backside mutters that this is the setter's lot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'My job' is the setter speaking: a crossword setter compiles puzzles.
explanation.definitionFit: The setter's work is to compile, assembling clues into a crossword.

clue.text: Crime, but not of dodgy dealer

indicators.note: the crime word without the small word that follows

explanation.surface: A crime, but not one committed by a shady trader.
explanation.definitionFit: A fence is a receiver of stolen goods, a criminal middleman who sells them on.

clue.text: Perhaps school bags always very hot

indicators.note: to bag something is to capture it, so the school word holds the other

parts.note: a school is a group of fish, hinted by perhaps

explanation.surface: A school seems to collect hot bags all the time.
explanation.definitionFit: Feverish describes having a high temperature, burning hot with fever.

clue.text: Good school subject to follow in French class

indicators.note: the subject comes after the French word

parts.note: RE is Religious Education, a school subject in Britain

explanation.surface: A good school subject follows on from a French lesson.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Class' looks like a school lesson but means a kind or category.
explanation.definitionFit: A genre is a category or kind, especially of artistic work, so it is a class.

clue.text: Person who digs up scripture about deity

parts.note: a miner digs up coal or ore

indicators.note: turned about means reversed

parts.note: AV is the Authorized Version of the Bible

explanation.surface: An archaeologist unearths scripture about a god.
explanation.definitionFit: Minerva is the Roman goddess of wisdom, a deity of the ancient pantheon.

clue.text: One having basic craft for a bit of carpentry

definitions.meaning: first meaning, read cryptically: someone on a raft, a basic boat
second meaning: a sloping beam in a roof frame

explanation.walkthrough: 'Craft' looks like skill but is a vessel.
explanation.definitionFit: A rafter is a timber beam supporting a roof, while a rafter is also a person riding a raft.

clue.text: Polish area of pan, vessel that's overturned

indicators.note: in a down answer, overturned means read upwards

parts.note: a wok is a Chinese pan

explanation.surface: A Polish kitchen where a pan and a pot have been tipped over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Polish' looks like the verb to shine, but it is the nationality.
explanation.definitionFit: Kraków is a city and province in southern Poland, a Polish region.

clue.text: He questionably claims penny on being given cash

explanation.surface: A dubious claimant puts a penny down when handed money.
explanation.definitionFit: A pretender asserts a claim, often to a throne, of doubtful legitimacy.

clue.text: Guarantee to lose right result

indicators.note: losing a letter drops it from the word

explanation.surface: A guaranteed lost right leads to a result.
explanation.definitionFit: To ensue is to follow as a consequence, to result from something.

clue.text: No bores providing film's opening shot

indicators.note: to bore is to drill into, so the negative goes inside
the opening of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: No bores, provided the film opens with a gunshot.
explanation.walkthrough: An in-off in snooker or billiards is a shot where the cue ball goes into a pocket off another ball.
explanation.definitionFit: An in-off is a billiards or snooker stroke, so it is a type of shot.

clue.text: York, say, has no hotel, but it does feature this

indicators.note: having no letter means it is dropped

parts.note: York is a royal house, as in the House of York

explanation.surface: York has no hotel, though it features something else.
explanation.walkthrough: 'York' looks like the city, but it is a royal dynasty; then the city returns in the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The River Ouse flows through the city of York, so York features it.

clue.text: Before request, take off a little winter covering

indicators.note: the skim word comes before the request

parts.note: to skim is to remove a thin layer from the top

explanation.surface: Before you ask, remove a bit of your winter wrapping.
explanation.definitionFit: A ski mask is a knitted hood covering the face against winter cold.

clue.text: Leader of police stops mastermind leaving home? He made many busts

indicators.note: to stop a gap is to fill it, so the letter is plugged into the gap
home leaves, so its letters are dropped
the leader of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A police chief halts a criminal mastermind leaving home, having made many arrests.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Busts' suggests police raids, but Jacob Epstein was a sculptor famous for portrait busts.
explanation.definitionFit: Sir Jacob Epstein was a sculptor whose bronze portrait heads were celebrated.

clue.text: Confession of follower heard to get slap

indicators.note: something heard is spoken, so these words are taken by sound

parts.note: a follower might confess I shadow, meaning I follow

explanation.surface: A follower's admission earns them a slap.
explanation.walkthrough: Slap is British slang for make-up.
explanation.definitionFit: Slap is slang for cosmetics, and eyeshadow is coloured make-up applied to the eyelids.
